einzeiler: A late-night encounter on the London embankment with a destitute man claiming to make…
kurzfassung: A weary narrator relaxing by the Thames is approached by a ragged, desperate man who claims to have successfully manufactured diamonds. Despite his impoverished appearance, the stranger produces an exceptionally large stone that easily scratches glass and offers to sell it. The narrator ultimately hesitates to buy or trust him fully, leaving behind a lifelong wonder about whether the man's unbelievable claims were true.
stichpunkte: The narrator meets a refined yet destitute man along the London embankment late at night.
The stranger startles the narrator by claiming that he manufactures large diamonds.
To prove his assertion, the man produces a massive, uncut octahedron that easily scratches a watch glass.
The diamond maker explains his decade-long obsession with discovering the correct carbon flux and immense pressure.
He recounts conducting dangerous high-pressure experiments inside a small, impoverished room using explosive cylinders.
After successfully extracting several large diamonds, a drunken neighbor's police report forced him to flee as a suspected anarchist.
Jewelers and receivers reject him out of suspicion, leaving him wandering London with a fortune he cannot cash.
The narrator declines to purchase the stone or pursue the opportunity, occasionally wondering ever since if he missed the chance of a lifetime.

clips.hook: A ragged tramp talking about the worries of a large business
clips.text: The narrator feels profound disbelief upon seeing a thoroughly unkempt and dirty stranger complain about the heavy burdens and anxieties of managing a major enterprise.
After testing the heavy, thumb-sized brown pebble against a watch glass and leaving a deep scratch, the narrator stares in rising astonishment at the impossible gem.

clips.hook: Devoting a life to artificial diamonds
clips.text: The creator describes spending thirteen years of his life single-mindedly pursuing the secret of crystallizing carbon into gems worth millions.
The experimenter details packing his chemical mixture and explosives into a heavy steel cylinder, building a roaring furnace fire, and casually leaving the house for a walk.

clips.hook: Wandering London with a fortune in his pocket
clips.text: The diamond maker explains his current predicament of roaming the streets hungry and shelterless while wearing hundreds of thousands of pounds around his neck.
